entities.summary:
Bonus was a Byzantine statesman and general who played a leading role in the successful defense of Constantinople during the Avar–Persian siege of 626.


Born into a noble family, Bonus served as a diplomat and strategist under Emperor Heraclius, who appointed him as the leader of the imperial forces defending the city. The siege, which lasted for 77 days, was the largest military campaign of the 7th century and saw the participation of various barbarian tribes, including the Avars and the Persians.


Bonus's leadership and military tactics were instrumental in repelling the siege, and he was subsequently awarded the title of 'Excellence' for his service.


His legacy as a skilled statesman and military commander has endured for centuries, and he remains one of the most important figures in Byzantine history.


As a testament to his enduring influence, the city of Thessaloniki in Greece still bears his name, a nod to his significant contributions to the city's defense and growth.
